newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar steady, arrivals from mills slow.
newsitem.headline: India sugar steady, arrivals from mills slow.

text.p: Indian sugar prices held steady in a narrow price range on the local market, dealers said.
Consumer demand as well as enquiries from the retailers remained slow at the tail end of the month but limited arrivals kept prices steady.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 was quiet at 1,415/1,455 rupees per quintal while M-30 was steady at 1,460/1,490 rupees per quintal.
"Arrivals of sugar from mills to the Bombay market remained low as most of millers have already sold their allotted quantity of free sale quota from the current month,"one broker said.

"Free sale quota for May is 800,000 tonnes against 750,000 tonnes released in April. Quota for June is 800,000 tonnes and major players in the market are awaiting state-wise allocation by the government of the sugar out of June's free sale quota," he said.

As millers have already sold their quantity of quota, trading in the mill delivery remained at a low ebb today and as soon as allotment for next month is announced, trading for mill delivery will start, he said.
